land.text: Fanteland round Mankessim, incorporated into the British Gold Coast

successors.note: Infobox: 'Incorporation into the British Gold Coast: 1873'. Cliopatria's british-gold-coast row starts in 1873; the Gold Coast page has the colony 'established on 24 July 1874'.

capitals.name: Mankessim
capitals.note: Infobox capital Mankessim; the Mankessim page gives 5°16′N 1°01′W and calls it the 'traditional headquarters' of the Fante.

correction.text: Fanteland on the central Gold Coast round Mankessim, from Winneba to Elmina

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area and no frontier and does not list the member states; the pages name Mankessim (capital), Abora, Anomabu, Cape Coast, Winneba (Ghartey IV), Abura, Twifo and Asen, Elmina (besieged) and Komenda. A 50 km circle at Mankessim (about 7,800 km2, part of it sea) reaches Winneba, Cape Coast, Anomabu and Elmina and is a stand-in, not a frontier.

ledger.note: January 1868: 'A January 1868 meeting at Mankessim included Fante paramount chiefs and representatives from Twifo and Asen' that 'declared the formation of the Fante Confederation', an independent state; Ghartey IV of Winneba elected first King-President. Infobox: 'Proclamation of the Fante Confederation: 1868'.

region.text: Komenda and the villages round Elmina

ledger.note: 1868: after the Dutch attack on Komenda in February 1868 the Confederation 'laid siege' to Elmina, 'but the campaign stalled' (page gives no further dates). The Dutch Gold Coast dossier (af-04-a) has the same contest from February 1868 and a peace with Elmina in June 1868. February is the Komenda attack the page names (the siege came after it); the page gives no month for the siege itself.

region.text: Komenda and the villages round Elmina

ledger.note: January 1870: the Dutch-led force 'laid the villages of Komenda, Anoema and Kwassie in ashes' in December 1869 and January 1870, and 'the events marked the end of Dutch involvement in the Gold Coast'. The page does not mention the Fante Confederacy or give a peace date; January 1870 is the end the Dutch dossier uses for the same contest. The Fante page says 'the Dutch sold their holdings to the British' in 1870 (the Gold Coast page gives 1872).

1873: 'collapsed by 1873 and Fanteland was fully incorporated' into the British Gold Coast. The page gives no month and no date for the British arrests of Fante leaders ('The British offered incentives to Fante leaders and arrested dissenters'); a revised constitution of November 1871 had made an Executive Council dominated by educated Fante merchants, with Amfo Otu sole head from 1872.

1873: the Confederacy ends (infobox: incorporation into the British Gold Coast 1873). The Gold Coast page puts the colony's establishment at 24 July 1874, after the Asante invasion of 1873 and the British occupation of Kumasi in January 1874.

wars.name: Fante Confederacy siege of Elmina
wars.outcome: The campaign 'stalled'; the Confederacy gained no ground on this page.
wars.note: The Dutch Gold Coast dossier dates the siege April-May 1868 and a peace treaty with Elmina in June 1868, from its Dutch Gold Coast page; the Fante page and the expedition page do not.

certainty.note: No frontier on any page; a circle round Mankessim.

notes: The Fante Confederacy has no Cliopatria row. Four pages; the Fante page is the only one that treats the Confederacy and it is thin: no area, no list of member states, no month for the siege of Elmina, no year for the arrests of leaders. Page conflicts: the Fante page says the Dutch sold their holdings in 1870 (the Gold Coast page and the Dutch dossier: 1872); the infobox predecessors (Bono State, Akani, Fetu Kingdom) are not used. The Mankessim page does not mention the Confederacy. Cliopatria's british-gold-coast row starts 1873, a year before the colony's 24 July 1874 establishment; the Fante land should be read as Fante-held until the Gold Coast row takes over. The 50 km circle is a stand-in; Fante lands also overlap the Dutch dossier's Elmina and the British forts of the Gold Coast settlements (Cape Coast Castle), which are not drawn here.
